title: What is known about 1RB1RA_1RC1LB, and what is open
description: Proof status of the six-state machine 1RB1RA_1RC1LB_1LD0RA_---0LE_1LC0LF_1RE0LB: what is proved in Lean, what is computed, what is only observed.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape. This page tracks what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.

The run's macro structure is now proved: Lean has the machine as an explicit map on lists of block lengths, and a theorem that the machine halts exactly when that map's run reaches one specific shape. What is open is whether it ever does. Read four macro steps at a time, the map is a carry wave running left through the blocks, and the halting shape becomes one arithmetic event: a single number built from the blocks being a power of two.
verdict: The question is open, and it is now a question about a list map. Lean proves that one macro step of the machine (a phase of transfers, then a sweep to the right or a carry to the left) is an explicit function next on the lists of block lengths, step counts included, and that the machine halts from blank tape iff the macro run reaches a halt. A macro step halts exactly when the head's block is odd and, after the transfers, every block to the left of the head is 2.

Running that map, Lean's kernel proves no halt in the first 2·1010 steps, and with native_decide in the first 9·1013. In those runs the left list holds blocks in the hundreds of thousands, far from all 2s. What is missing is an argument that the map never produces that shape.

The halting condition in one number. Every fourth time A stands on the blank right of the tape, the tape is blocks p1, …, pm followed by 5, 0. With N = 10 + Σ pl·2m−l (the blocks read as binary digits), the next such time follows from an explicit formula in which a wave of halvings runs v2(N) + 1 blocks to the left. It reaches the left end of the tape when 2m−1 divides N, which explains why the head gets there so rarely, and the machine halts if and only if N is ever a power of two. This reformulation is computed (checked against direct simulation and against the proved macro map), not yet proved in Lean. Running it, there is no halt in 3.7·1022 steps.

claims.title: The machine halts iff the macro run does
claims.text: With X(ls, n, cs) = 0∞ 1lr 0 … 0 1l1 0 A> 1n 000 1c1 00 … 00 1cs 0∞, the run from blank tape is at X([1], 2, []) after 15 steps, and from every X the machine goes where the list function next says, in exactly the steps it says (next_sound). Every reachable X is well formed, so the machine halts from blank tape iff the macro run runM reaches a halt (halts_iff).

claims.title: When a macro step halts
claims.text: A macro step from X(k :: ls, n, cs) halts iff n is odd and every block of (k + ⌊n/2⌋) :: ls equals 2: the carry to the left eats every block of 2 and reaches the left end.

claims.title: Seven block rules
claims.text: Transfer (two cells of the head's block move, one left, one right, 2n + 11 steps), the start and each block of the sweep to the right, and the four stages of the carry to the left; each for every block length and any surrounding tape.

claims.title: No halt in 2·10<sup>10</sup> steps
claims.text: 10<sup>5</sup> macro steps from blank tape, evaluated by Lean's kernel, take more than 2·10<sup>10</sup> machine steps without a halt. (Step by step, the kernel checks 20,000.)

claims.title: Two shift rules
claims.text: State A runs right over a block of n ones in n steps; state B runs left over a block of n ones to the 0 before it in n + 1 steps; for every n and any surrounding tape.

claims.title: No halt in 9·10<sup>13</sup> steps
claims.text: 10<sup>7</sup> macro steps, by compiled evaluation: more than 9·10<sup>13</sup> machine steps without a halt. (Step by step: 10,000,000.)

claims.title: The Python macro model
claims.text: py/macro.py computes the same map; it is tested against the reference simulator at every macro configuration of the first 1,000 macro steps (1,322,171 machine steps, the same count Lean's runM_1000 gives) and on built configurations that halt.

claims.title: No simple conserved quantity
claims.text: No quantity a·(number of 1s) + b·(head position) + W[state] is conserved modulo any m from 2 to 12. (The other machine has one modulo 3, which the same search finds.)

claims.title: The wave model and the halting criterion
claims.text: py/waves.py: each time A stands on the blank right of the tape, the next such time follows from the block lengths by a left-going wave, with exact step counts; every fourth time the tape is [p1, …, pm, 5, 0], and with dm+1 = 20, dl = pl + dl+1/2 the wave turns at the last odd di. The machine halts iff N = 10 + Σ pl·2m−l is ever a power of two. Checked against tmrun at all 12,927 such times of the first 109 steps, against every new left cell up to 1010 steps, and against the first 2,000 configurations of the proved macro map.

claims.title: The next return to the left end
claims.text: After step 2,047,931 the head next reaches new tape on the left at step 26,618,972,322, as the wave model predicted; a direct run to 2.7·10<sup>10</sup> steps confirms it and finds no other new left cell in between.

claims.title: No halt in 3.7·10<sup>22</sup> steps
claims.text: The wave model in C (128-bit step counts) runs 7·10<sup>10</sup> macro steps without a halt. The wave reaches the left end 16 times on the way, never with N a power of two. Rests on the wave model.

claims.title: Far from the halting shape
claims.text: In 10<sup>7</sup> macro steps the left list of blocks holds blocks in the hundreds of thousands; halting needs every block to the left of the head to be 2.

claims.title: Why the returns to the left end are rare
claims.text: The wave is a binary carry: reaching the left end needs v<sub>2</sub>(N) ≥ m − 1, about once in 2<sup>m−1</sup> super steps if N's low bits behave like coin flips, and each return adds blocks. The observed gaps fit that estimate to within a factor of two. The returns do not stop; they thin out.

claims.title: Almost certainly no halt
claims.text: At a return the deciding number is now about 10<sup>9</sup> and grows; if it behaved like a random integer, the chance of ever hitting a power of two would be far below 10<sup>−6</sup>. N shows no modular obstruction (all residues mod 3 to 21 occur).

claims.title: Whether it halts
claims.text: Whether the macro run ever reaches an X with n odd and every left block (after the transfers) equal to 2. Equivalently: whether N = 10 + Σ p<sub>l</sub>·2<sup>m−l</sup> is ever a power of two along the run, a Collatz-like question about one orbit.

python3 bb6-1RB1RA_1RC1LB/tests/test_waves.py   # the wave model against direct simulation (about 25 s)
